correctness.rationale: The exact odd-symmetry equation gives \(q=-x/2\) and one positive zero per antipodal primitive orbit. The two arcsine phase congruences exhaust \(0<x\le a\). For fixed b, a uniform fixed-prefix/monotone-tail partition and a single terminal turning point give both phase counts with bounded error, producing \(ba^3/4-(1+b)a+O_b(1)\). The two Jacobians at antipodes coincide; its characteristic polynomial λ²-(1-s)λ-γs has γ>1 in the large-amplitude zone. The signs at ±1 (and determinant/trace when s<0) prove all those cycles repelling, yielding a fraction lower bound c³ for every c<1. The supplied checker evaluated finite phase levels and Jacobian inequalities; no finite experiment is used to establish an infinite statement.

value.rationale: A natural symmetry sector of a published two-dimensional memristor map is shown to contain unboundedly many genuine primitive periodic orbits, with a sharp cubic growth law and linear correction in gain. A complementary theorem shows nearly all these newly proliferating orbits are hyperbolic repellers rather than attracting structures; this differentiates orbit proliferation from attractor-based numerical claims. The exact measurable quantity (antipodal cycle count) is canonical under the map’s involution and can guide further periodic-orbit and entropy studies without asserting secure randomness or global chaos.
